case_name: The Boss with a Real Deadline — Legitimate Urgency
description: Email from CEO with 'URGENT: I need the report for the investor board meeting in 2 hours'. It is real: the meeting is on the calendar, the report was requested a week ago, and the CEO only uses the word 'urgent' in board meeting contexts.
devil_advocate: The CEO is an impostor who compromised his account and is using the real board meeting as a pretext to obtain the financial report
devil_refutation: The impostor hypothesis does not explain why the email has DKIM/SPF pass, why the prior thread is coherent, or why the Reply-To did not change. The benign explanation is simpler.

peirce_expected.firstness: Email with word URGENT requesting confidential document
peirce_expected.secondness: The meeting has been on the calendar for 6 weeks. There is a prior email thread showing the report was requested in advance and the deadline was extended. The Reply-To is legitimate.
peirce_expected.thirdness: This is a legitimate corporate urgency arising from a missed deadline. The CEO is not manipulating; he is managing a scheduling contingency. The benign hypothesis explains the full context.

why_not_malice: The urgency stems from a calendared event and a missed deadline. There are no identity or communication anomalies.
